_comment: The dimensions a text varies along. Each tag belongs to one side: augmentation (a family of jailbreak/combination_spec.json, which transforms a finished text) or generation (an axis of generation_axes.json, which shapes a text as it is written). Each family and each axis carries one tag as dimension; the definition says what property of the text it varies. A generation tag may list in same_as the augmentation tags that are the same dimension, and in undecided those the owner has yet to rule on, checked as the same until then. A run stops before any stage when an axis that varies (one with from, or with two or more values of weight above 0) and a family a kind draws share a dimension. Read by redact/dimensions.py.

language.definition: The natural language the message is written in, or asks to be answered in.

surface_noise.definition: Variation in spelling, casing, spacing, punctuation and added symbols that leaves the meaning of every word as it was.

encoding.definition: The written form of some or all of the message's characters or words, when it is other than plain text in the message's own alphabet.

semantic_form.definition: A reformulation that re-expresses the request's meaning in another symbolic or literary form (a symbolic-math problem, verse, an acrostic hidden in a benign paragraph, or an information-overload restatement) while keeping it recoverable.

container.definition: A data format, markup or document structure that the finished message is placed inside.

role_framing.definition: A role, character or invented scenario set up in the message, for its writer or its reader, around the request.

request_shape.definition: The frame a finished request is put in: its tense, a task or passage it is set within, and other text placed before or after it.

answer_shape.definition: What the message asks of the answer's form: its format, layout or opening.

example_priming.definition: Example exchanges placed in the message before the request.

authorship.definition: Who the writer is, as their role or situation shows in what they ask and how, never offered as a reason to be answered.

request_intent.definition: The act the writer's own request performs (an instruction, a question, a request for advice, a statement, a request for an opinion) and how plainly it names its subject.

length.definition: How long the message is, from a few words to a document.

register.definition: The formality, expertise and feeling of the message's word choice and sentence construction.

focus.definition: Whether the subject fills the whole message or is one part of a message also about other things.

domain.definition: The subject area of the taxonomy that the message is about.

answer_layout.definition: The visual structure of the response: prose, a list, numbered steps, headed sections, a table or a code block.

answer_tone.definition: The formality, warmth and expertise of the response's wording.
